- Led by: the product manager seat (fresh context, pm-rerank-9; Claude because the probes at 17:13 UTC in .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota). Window: 208-rerank-9 (D153); every declared role polled (architect, QA engineer, backend developer, independent reviewer (audit lens), delivery lead, product manager (signoff)); D158 checklist in the window file.
- Before (note 8b): 208, 210, 211, 219, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207; unranked 220 to 225.
- After: 208 (a seat starts only on a fresh, pinned probe; MD-002), 210 (record checker; MD-003), 211 (MD-010 corrective), 220 (loop starts a corrective card while a finding blocks), 221 (loop runs a card in its Repository line's repository), 222 (loop wires retro and re-rank steps and stops on failure), 223 (per-card retro from every role), 224 (re-rank through the product manager and a Decider), 225 (card mode reads only role lines), 219, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207.
- Next card: 208 (the seat probe gate, corrective for MD-002 and F-008; the window 208-slice order puts it first because it is the only silent staffing drift and the only FAIL among the five gaps).
- Gate (stop-the-line): can start now, each names an open finding: 208 (MD-002), 210 (MD-003), 211 (MD-010), 220 to 225 (F-008). Cannot start while MD-002, MD-003, MD-010 or F-008 is open: 219, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207. Per D160 no exemption for 219, which stays after the corrective cards.
- Changed: six new cards enter ranks 4 to 9 in the order of the 208-slice (which gap, once enforced, stops the most drift first): the loop corrective gate (220), the repository (221), the steps and stop on failure (222), then retro (223) and re-rank (224), which depend on 208 and 222 and so come after both, then role lines (225), a loud refusal with a one-line workaround. 219 moves from fourth to tenth: it follows all corrective cards (D160), and F-008 stays open until 225 lands. 217 to 207 keep their relative order.
- Cost: 220 is worth more than 210 and 211 for the loop (without it the loop stops on every corrective card), but D160 C3 reasoning (the checker compares a close with the next-lower card number's record, so an out-of-order corrective close is refused) keeps number order 208, 210, 211, 220 to 225. Risk to watch: 220 to 225 sit above card 219 in number, so their records may be refused until 219 lands, as 209's held record is (blocker 2026-10-30-209-record-order, D159); if the checker refuses, the delivery lead raises a blocker and the mob does not skip the order. Any slice change that contradicts this is a task-force question, not a rank change.
- Evidence considered: D161 (product owner direction: rules enforced in the template and the loop runner first); D160 (208 before 210, no exemption, 219 after the corrective cards); audit 42 open FAILs MD-002, MD-003, MD-010; the 208-slice section 1 order; the six drafted cards' stated dependencies (223 and 224 on 208 and 222); the probes at 17:13 UTC.
- Rationale (one line): the lock-down cards, in order of the process gaps they stop (a seat probe gate (208), the record checker (210), the MD-010 fix (211), the loop's corrective-card gate (220), repository (221), steps (222), retro (223), re-rank (224), role lines (225)), rank ahead of all product work, and number order is kept because the gate can start only corrective cards and the record checker refuses out-of-order closes before the record-order card (219) lands.
